records.context: ``'well_set'``: the :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` on per-cell embeddings, scored by mechanism of action with its ablations and controls (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#2
records.source: ``'well_set'``: the :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` on per-cell embeddings, scored by mechanism of action with its ablations and controls (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).
records.translation: ``'well_set'``: el :class:`spacr.channel_models.SpacrWellTransformer` sobre incrustaciones por célula, puntuado por mecanismo de acción con sus ablaciones y controles (:func:`spacr.well_set_training.run_well_set_training`).

records.context: ``'cell'``: the image data channel-adaptive CNN or ViT (``train_arch``) on single-cell extracted image regions (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Optionally the ViT is first pre-trained without labels (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, or ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) for ``pretrain_epochs`` epochs; ``train_labels_per_class`` then keeps only that many labelled cells per class (few-shot). Every model is scored on the full stain panel and on each subset of ``eval_channel_subsets`` (the missing-stain evaluation), beside a majority-class control and, with ``train_set_shuffle_control``, a model trained on shuffled labels.
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#3
records.source: ``'cell'``: the channel-adaptive CNN or ViT (``train_arch``) on single-cell crops (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Optionally the ViT is first pre-trained without labels (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, or ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) for ``pretrain_epochs`` epochs; ``train_labels_per_class`` then keeps only that many labelled cells per class (few-shot). Every model is scored on the full stain panel and on each subset of ``eval_channel_subsets`` (the missing-stain evaluation), beside a majority-class control and, with ``train_set_shuffle_control``, a model trained on shuffled labels.
records.translation: ``'cell'``: la CNN o el ViT adaptativos al canal (``train_arch``) sobre recortes de células individuales (:func:`run_cell_architecture`). Opcionalmente, el ViT se preentrena primero sin etiquetas (``pretrain_method``: ``'mae'``, He et al. 2022, o ``'dino'``, Caron et al. 2021) durante ``pretrain_epochs`` épocas; ``train_labels_per_class`` conserva entonces solo ese número de células etiquetadas por clase (few-shot). Cada modelo se puntúa con el panel completo de tinciones y con cada subconjunto de ``eval_channel_subsets`` (la evaluación con tinciones ausentes), junto a un control de clase mayoritaria y, con ``train_set_shuffle_control``, un modelo entrenado con etiquetas barajadas.

records.context: Cell extracted image regions come as one ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` array (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) with a row-aligned table (``train_cell_table``) holding the label and the group (well) column; cells are split by group, so no well is in both training and test. The extracted image regions are raw: each image data channel is divided by the 99th percentile of up to 2,048 training extracted image regions, clipped at 1.5 and mapped by ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, the transform of the gene-class benchmark. Training augments by flips, 90-degree rotations and a per-image data channel gain within 10%.
records.label: spacr.architecture_training#4
records.source: Cell crops come as one ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` array (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) with a row-aligned table (``train_cell_table``) holding the label and the group (well) column; cells are split by group, so no well is in both training and test. The crops are raw: each channel is divided by the 99th percentile of up to 2,048 training crops, clipped at 1.5 and mapped by ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, the transform of the gene-class benchmark. Training augments by flips, 90-degree rotations and a per-channel gain within 10%.
records.translation: Los recortes celulares llegan como una matriz ``(cells, channels, height, width)`` (``train_cell_crops``, ``.npy``) con una tabla alineada por filas (``train_cell_table``) que contiene la etiqueta y la columna de grupo (pocillo); las células se dividen por grupo, de modo que ningún pocillo está a la vez en entrenamiento y en prueba. Los recortes están sin procesar: cada canal se divide por el percentil 99 de hasta 2,048 recortes de entrenamiento, se recorta en 1.5 y se transforma con ``(x - 0.5) / 0.25``, la transformación del banco de pruebas de clases génicas. El entrenamiento aumenta los datos con volteos, rotaciones de 90 grados y una ganancia por canal dentro del 10%.

records.context: Image data channel-adaptive models for any stain panel: a CNN, a ViT and a microplate sample position set transformer.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#0
records.source: Channel-adaptive models for any stain panel: a CNN, a ViT and a well set transformer.
records.translation: Modelos adaptativos al canal para cualquier panel de tinciones: una CNN, un ViT y un transformador de conjuntos de pocillos.

records.context: All three models take any number of image data channels (1 to more than 10) with the same weights. Every image data channel is processed on its own and tagged with a learned stain embedding, looked up by stain name rather than by slot index, so BBBC021 "DNA" and an OPS "DAPI" share one vector and an unseen panel still runs.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#1
records.source: All three models take any number of channels (1 to more than 10) with the same weights. Every channel is processed on its own and tagged with a learned stain embedding, looked up by stain name rather than by slot index, so BBBC021 "DNA" and an OPS "DAPI" share one vector and an unseen panel still runs.
records.translation: Los tres modelos aceptan cualquier número de canales (de 1 a más de 10) con los mismos pesos. Cada canal se procesa por separado y se marca con una incrustación de tinción aprendida, buscada por nombre de tinción y no por índice de posición, de modo que "DNA" de BBBC021 y un "DAPI" de OPS comparten un vector y un panel no visto sigue funcionando.

records.context: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` is an image data channel-adaptive ConvNeXt-style CNN: a HyperNet stem per image data channel, ConvNeXt blocks shared across image data channels and FiLM-conditioned on the stain, cross-image data channel attention at every spatial location (one feature map per image data channel is kept) and image data channel attention pooling at the end, which records the stain that drove the call.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#2
records.source: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` is a channel-adaptive ConvNeXt-style CNN: a HyperNet stem per channel, ConvNeXt blocks shared across channels and FiLM-conditioned on the stain, cross-channel attention at every spatial location (one feature map per channel is kept) and channel attention pooling at the end, which records the stain that drove the call.
records.translation: :class:`SpacrChannelCNN` es una CNN adaptativa al canal de estilo ConvNeXt: un tallo HyperNet por canal, bloques ConvNeXt compartidos entre canales y condicionados por FiLM a la tinción, atención entre canales en cada posición espacial (se conserva un mapa de características por canal) y agrupación por atención de canales al final, que registra la tinción que determinó la predicción.

records.context: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` is an image data channel-aware ViT: per-image data channel patch tokens plus a stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position, an optional per-sample image data channel-availability mask for missing stains, and Hierarchical image data channel Sampling (image data channel dropout, Bao et al. 2024) in training. It is pre-trained with :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) or :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).
records.label: spacr.channel_models#3
records.source: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` is a channel-aware ViT: per-channel patch tokens plus a stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position, an optional per-sample channel-availability mask for missing stains, and Hierarchical Channel Sampling (channel dropout, Bao et al. 2024) in training. It is pre-trained with :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) or :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).
records.translation: :class:`SpacrChannelViT` es un ViT consciente del canal: tokens de parche por canal más una incrustación de tinción y una posición seno-coseno 2-D, una máscara opcional de disponibilidad de canales por muestra para tinciones ausentes, y Hierarchical Channel Sampling (dropout de canales, Bao et al. 2024) en el entrenamiento. Se preentrena con :class:`ChannelMAE` (He et al. 2022) o :class:`ChannelDINO` (Caron et al. 2021).

records.context: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` is a set model over the single-cell embeddings of a well. Mode ``'arrayed'``: an ISAB set encoder (Lee et al. 2019) and gated multi-head attention-MIL pooling (Ilse et al. 2018) give the well logits, the attention weights and per-cell instance logits (the penetrant fraction, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Mode ``'pooled'``: per-cell logits conditioned on a context set of other cells of the same well; an empty context is a learned null token, so the no-context ablation is the same model with set size 0.
records.label: spacr.channel_models#4
records.source: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` is a set model over the single-cell embeddings of a well. Mode ``'arrayed'``: an ISAB set encoder (Lee et al. 2019) and gated multi-head attention-MIL pooling (Ilse et al. 2018) give the well logits, the attention weights and per-cell instance logits (the penetrant fraction, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Mode ``'pooled'``: per-cell logits conditioned on a context set of other cells of the same well; an empty context is a learned null token, so the no-context ablation is the same model with set size 0.
records.translation: :class:`SpacrWellTransformer` es un modelo de conjuntos sobre las incrustaciones de células individuales de un pocillo. Modo ``'arrayed'``: un codificador de conjuntos ISAB (Lee et al. 2019) y una agrupación attention-MIL multicabeza con compuerta (Ilse et al. 2018) dan los logits del pocillo, los pesos de atención y logits de instancia por célula (la fracción penetrante, :func:`penetrant_fraction`). Modo ``'pooled'``: logits por célula condicionados a un conjunto de contexto de otras células del mismo pocillo; un contexto vacío es un token nulo aprendido, de modo que la ablación sin contexto es el mismo modelo con tamaño de conjunto 0.

records.translation: :func:`build_channel_model` es el registro: construye cualquiera de los tres por el nombre en :data:`CHANNEL_ARCHITECTURES`, que es también lo que aceptan el ajuste de entrenamiento ``train_arch`` y :func:`spacr.utils.choose_model`. :class:`ChannelClassifier` da a los dos modelos de imagen la interfaz ``model(x) -> logits`` del resto de la ruta de entrenamiento de spaCR.

records.source: Inputs are expected already normalised by the benchmark transform, ``((x / scale).clip(0, 1.5) - 0.5) / 0.25``. The models use plain torch modules and no BatchNorm, so a step with a zero learning rate leaves every weight unchanged.
records.translation: Se espera que las entradas ya estén normalizadas con la transformación del banco de pruebas, ``((x / scale).clip(0, 1.5) - 0.5) / 0.25``. records.context: ``mask_ratio`` of all ``C * N`` tokens is masked at random, and with probability ``p_whole_channel`` per sample one whole image data channel is masked in addition, so the model learns to predict one stain from the others. The loss is the mean squared error on the masked patches, each patch normalised to zero mean and unit variance.
records.label: spacr.channel_models.ChannelMAE#1
records.source: ``mask_ratio`` of all ``C * N`` tokens is masked at random, and with probability ``p_whole_channel`` per sample one whole channel is masked in addition, so the model learns to predict one stain from the others. One decoder is shared by all channels; the stain embedding tells it which to paint. The loss is the mean squared error on the masked patches, each patch normalised to zero mean and unit variance.
records.translation: Se enmascara al azar ``mask_ratio`` de todos los ``C * N`` tokens y, con probabilidad ``p_whole_channel`` por muestra, se enmascara además un canal completo, de modo que el modelo aprende a predecir una tinción a partir de las demás. Todos los canales comparten un decodificador; la incrustación de tinción le indica cuál pintar. La pérdida es el error cuadrático medio en los parches enmascarados, con cada parche normalizado a media cero y varianza unitaria.

In training, with ``channel_dropout``, a random channel subset is kept per batch (the ``always_keep`` stains are never dropped). records.translation: Tamaño predeterminado: dims (32, 64, 128, 256), depths (2, 2, 4, 2), unos 2.4 M de parámetros. La altura y la anchura deben ser divisibles por 32 (96, 128 y 224 funcionan). En el entrenamiento, con ``channel_dropout``, se conserva un subconjunto aleatorio de canales por lote (las tinciones de ``always_keep`` nunca se descartan). En la prueba, ``eval_channel_subset`` conserva solo las tinciones nombradas, la evaluación con tinciones ausentes.

records.context: Tokens: one shared one-image data channel patch embedding per image data channel, plus the stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position shared over image data channels, so ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens and a CLS token. Default img 224 and patch 32 (49 tokens per image data channel). The native-resolution arm is img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) or img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). With ``bag_of_channels`` every image data channel is a separate sequence and the per-image data channel CLS vectors are fused late, which is cheaper and the better self-supervised setting on CHAMMI-75.
records.label: spacr.channel_models.SpacrChannelViT#1
records.source: Tokens: one shared one-channel patch embedding per channel, plus the stain embedding and a 2-D sin-cos position shared over channels, so ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens and a CLS token. Default img 224 and patch 32 (49 tokens per channel). The native-resolution arm is img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) or img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). With ``bag_of_channels`` every channel is a separate sequence and the per-channel CLS vectors are fused late, which is cheaper and the better self-supervised setting on CHAMMI-75.
records.translation: Tokens: una incrustación de parche de un canal compartida por canal, más la incrustación de tinción y una posición seno-coseno 2-D compartida entre canales, es decir, ``C * (img / patch) ** 2`` tokens y un token CLS. Por defecto img 224 y patch 32 (49 tokens por canal). El brazo de resolución nativa es img 96 / patch 12 (OPS) o img 128 / patch 16 (BBBC021). Con ``bag_of_channels`` cada canal es una secuencia separada y los vectores CLS por canal se fusionan tarde, lo que es más barato y es la mejor configuración autosupervisada en CHAMMI-75.

records.context: The nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 machine-learning classification models, built as CellProfiler Analyst builds them.
records.label: spacr.cpa_classifiers#0
records.source: The nine CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 classifiers, built as CellProfiler Analyst builds them.
records.translation: Los nueve clasificadores de CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5, construidos como los construye CellProfiler Analyst.

records.context: CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, version 3.0.5, BSD 3-Clause licence, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) offers nine machine-learning classification models in its machine-learning classification model window. Eight are scikit-learn estimators that CPA's ``GeneralClassifier`` constructs from a fixed string, with an optional :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fitted on the training data; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` holds the strings and scaler flags verbatim from ``cpa/classifier.py``. The ninth, FastGentleBoosting, is CPA's own boosted stumps (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", ieee pami), ported here from ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` with the same arithmetic in ``float32``, the same unstable ``argsort`` and the same tie rule, and scored as CPA scores cells (sum over rules of ``a`` if ``x > threshold`` else ``b``, argmax).
records.label: spacr.cpa_classifiers#1
records.source: CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, version 3.0.5, BSD 3-Clause licence, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) offers nine classifiers in its Classifier window. Eight are scikit-learn estimators that CPA's ``GeneralClassifier`` constructs from a fixed string, with an optional :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` fitted on the training data; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` holds the strings and scaler flags verbatim from ``cpa/classifier.py``. The ninth, FastGentleBoosting, is CPA's own boosted stumps (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", IEEE PAMI), ported here from ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` with the same arithmetic in ``float32``, the same unstable ``argsort`` and the same tie rule, and scored as CPA scores cells (sum over rules of ``a`` if ``x > threshold`` else ``b``, argmax).
records.translation: CellProfiler Analyst (CPA; github.com/CellProfiler/CellProfiler-Analyst, commit f5e1b5e2b2c35bb1aff4516ae5a49fe420df0350, versión 3.0.5, licencia BSD 3-Clause, Copyright 2003-2024 Broad Institute) ofrece nueve clasificadores en su ventana Classifier. Ocho son estimadores de scikit-learn que el ``GeneralClassifier`` de CPA construye a partir de una cadena fija, con un :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` opcional ajustado a los datos de entrenamiento; :data:`CPA_GENERAL` contiene las cadenas y los indicadores del escalador literalmente de ``cpa/classifier.py``. El noveno, FastGentleBoosting, son los tocones potenciados propios de CPA (Torralba et al. 2007, "Sharing visual features for multiclass and multiview object detection", IEEE PAMI), portados aquí desde ``cpa/fastgentleboosting.py`` con la misma aritmética en ``float32``, el mismo ``argsort`` inestable y la misma regla de desempate, y puntuados como CPA puntúa las células (suma sobre las reglas de ``a`` si ``x > threshold`` y si no ``b``, argmax).

records.context: :func:`make_cpa_model` returns an estimator with ``fit``, ``predict`` and ``predict_proba``; :func:`spacr.moa_benchmark.loco_supervised` fits it as ``cpa_<name>``, such as ``cpa_RandomForestClassifier``. A machine-learning classification model that takes a ``random_state`` gets the fold's seed, as the BBBC021 reanalysis (``cpa_models.py``) set it. FastGentleBoosting has no probabilities: its additive scores go through a softmax so that averaging over a treatment's microplate sample positions is defined.

A classifier that takes a ``random_state`` gets the fold's seed, as the BBBC021 reanalysis (``cpa_models.py``) set it. FastGentleBoosting has no probabilities: its additive scores go through a softmax so that averaging over a treatment's wells is defined.

records.context: The computer-vision arm of the BBBC021 benchmark, from settings, in four steps that :func:`run_embedding_profiles` runs in order:
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles#1
records.source: The computer-vision arm of the BBBC021 benchmark, from settings, in four steps that :func:`run_embedding_profiles` runs in order:
records.translation: El brazo de visión por computador del banco de pruebas BBBC021, a partir de ajustes, en cuatro pasos que :func:`run_embedding_profiles` ejecuta en orden:

records.context: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` cuts a fixed-size window around each chosen cell of a laboratory microplate from its merged microscope fields of view (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), raw: never stretched per extracted image region (item 772), optionally divided by the laboratory microplate's saved flat microscope field of view (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), with a bit-flag mask (1 this cell, 2 any nucleus, 4 another cell, 8 outside the microscope field of view). At most ``crop_cap_per_well`` cells per microplate sample position are drawn by ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, microplate sample position by microplate sample position in sorted order. One HDF5 shard per laboratory microplate holds ``images`` and ``masks``, beside a ``.cells.parquet`` with one row per extracted image region; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` encodes the masked extracted image regions with a pretrained backbone (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), each image data channel alone, under one fixed scale per laboratory microplate and image data channel (the 99th percentile of a 2,048-extracted image region sample, item 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` writes ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` and the control cells' percentiles in the layout of the feature aggregate (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), so :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` scores them unchanged; 4. :func:`well_umap` writes a UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) of the microplate sample positions.
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles#2
records.source: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` cuts a fixed-size window around each chosen cell of a plate from its merged fields (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), raw: never stretched per crop (item 772), optionally divided by the plate's saved flat field (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), with a bit-flag mask (1 this cell, 2 any nucleus, 4 another cell, 8 outside the field). At most ``crop_cap_per_well`` cells per well are drawn by ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, well by well in sorted order. One HDF5 shard per plate holds ``images`` and ``masks``, beside a ``.cells.parquet`` with one row per crop; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` encodes the masked crops with a pretrained backbone (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), each channel alone, under one fixed scale per plate and channel (the 99th percentile of a 2,048-crop sample, item 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` writes ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` and the control cells' percentiles in the layout of the feature aggregate (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), so :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` scores them unchanged; 4. :func:`well_umap` writes a UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) of the wells.
records.translation: 1. :func:`write_crop_shard` corta una ventana de tamaño fijo alrededor de cada célula elegida de una placa a partir de sus campos fusionados (:func:`spacr.crops.open_merged_field`), sin procesar: nunca estirada por recorte (ítem 772), opcionalmente dividida por el campo plano guardado de la placa (``crop_illumination='gain_offset'``), con una máscara de indicadores de bits (1 esta célula, 2 cualquier núcleo, 4 otra célula, 8 fuera del campo). Se sortean como máximo ``crop_cap_per_well`` células por pocillo con ``numpy.random.default_rng(crop_seed)``, pocillo a pocillo en orden. Un fragmento HDF5 por placa contiene ``images`` y ``masks``, junto a un ``.cells.parquet`` con una fila por recorte; 2. :func:`embed_crop_shard` codifica los recortes enmascarados con una red troncal preentrenada (:mod:`spacr.embeddings`), cada canal por separado, con una escala fija por placa y canal (el percentil 99 de una muestra de 2,048 recortes, ítem 410); 3. :func:`aggregate_embedding_wells` escribe ``wells_median.parquet``, ``wells_mean.parquet`` y los percentiles de las células control con la disposición del agregado de características (:func:`spacr.screen_staging.aggregate_wells`), de modo que :func:`spacr.sp_stats.moa_evaluation` los puntúa sin cambios; 4. :func:`well_umap` escribe un UMAP (McInnes et al. 2018) de los pocillos.

records.context: For each cell the window of side ``size`` centred on its rounded centroid in the ``cell`` label image layer is read from ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (zero padded past the edge). With ``illumination`` the laboratory microplate's flat field is applied as Measure applies it: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, clipped to uint16 and the clipped pixels counted. ``mask_flags`` adds the bit mask of :data:`MASK_BITS`. Writes ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` and ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, chunks of 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (the cells in shard order with ``row``, centroid, bounding box, mask area, clipped pixels and ``truncated``) and ``<plate>.json``.
records.label: spacr.embedding_profiles.write_crop_shard#1
records.source: For each cell the window of side ``size`` centred on its rounded centroid in the ``cell`` label plane is read from ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (zero padded past the edge). With ``illumination`` the plate's flat field is applied as Measure applies it: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, clipped to uint16 and the clipped pixels counted. ``mask_flags`` adds the bit mask of :data:`MASK_BITS`. Writes ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` and ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, chunks of 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (the cells in shard order with ``row``, centroid, bounding box, mask area, clipped pixels and ``truncated``) and ``<plate>.json``.
records.translation: Para cada célula, la ventana de lado ``size`` centrada en su centroide redondeado en el plano de etiquetas ``cell`` se lee de ``merged/<plate>_<well>_<site>_1.npy`` (rellenada con ceros más allá del borde). Con ``illumination``, el campo plano de la placa se aplica como lo aplica Measure: ``rint((window - offset) * gain)``, recortado a uint16 y con los píxeles recortados contados. ``mask_flags`` añade la máscara de bits de :data:`MASK_BITS`. Escribe ``<out>/<plate>.h5`` (``images`` uint16 ``(n, size, size, channels)`` y ``masks`` uint8, gzip 4, bloques de 32), ``<plate>.cells.parquet`` (las células en el orden del fragmento con ``row``, centroide, recuadro delimitador, área de la máscara, píxeles recortados y ``truncated``) y ``<plate>.json``.

records.translation: Esta es la mitad de imagen del ítem 889, portada desde ``gc_train.py`` del reanálisis BMC para que un fold del banco de pruebas o piloto sea una ejecución de spaCR. Un fold:

records.context: 1. the extracted image regions: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, a ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 ``.npy`` with an index table holding ``scale0..`` per cell) or :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, cell-masked TIFF extracted image regions in tar shards with ``.index.csv`` byte offsets and a per-laboratory microplate scale file). Both divide by a fixed per-laboratory microplate, per-image data channel scale and clip, so extracted image regions stay raw on disk; 2. the labels and folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (MoA classes and the NSCB / NSC folds of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) or :func:`ops_fold_setup` (multi-label gene classes from the :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` tables, gene folds, decoy heads, the shuffled control and the per-gene loss weight); 3. the sampler (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, class-uniform for BBBC021 and, for OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (half the batch from positive genes, class then gene then cell; half from negative genes); 4. the model (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` with the first convolution adapted to the image data channel count (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. the transform: :func:`transform_spec` records the whole preprocessing, which is saved with the fold and checked again before scoring (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` applies it on the device, with the train-time augmentation (dihedral, shift of up to 4 px, per-image data channel gain 0.9 to 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` trains with AdamW and a cosine schedule (AMP on a GPU, micro-batch halving on out-of-memory) and scores the held-out cells; :func:`score_bbbc_run` scores a BBBC021 run per microplate sample position and per treatment.

records.source: 1. the crops: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, a ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 ``.npy`` with an index table holding ``scale0..`` per cell) or :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, cell-masked TIFF crops in tar shards with ``.index.csv`` byte offsets and a per-plate scale file). Both divide by a fixed per-plate, per-channel scale and clip, so crops stay raw on disk; 2. the labels and folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (MoA classes and the NSCB / NSC folds of :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) or :func:`ops_fold_setup` (multi-label gene classes from the :mod:`spacr.gene_classes` tables, gene folds, decoy heads, the shuffled control and the per-gene loss weight); 3. the sampler (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, class-uniform for BBBC021 and, for OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (half the batch from positive genes, class then gene then cell; half from negative genes); 4. the model (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` with the first convolution adapted to the channel count (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. the transform: :func:`transform_spec` records the whole preprocessing, which is saved with the fold and checked again before scoring (:func:`check_transform`, item 772). :class:`DevicePrep` applies it on the device, with the train-time augmentation (dihedral, shift of up to 4 px, per-channel gain 0.9 to 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` trains with AdamW and a cosine schedule (AMP on a GPU, micro-batch halving on out-of-memory) and scores the held-out cells; :func:`score_bbbc_run` scores a BBBC021 run per well and per treatment.
records.translation: 1. los recortes: :class:`MemmapCrops` (BBBC021, una matriz ``(cells, H, W, C)`` uint16 ``.npy`` con una tabla de índice que contiene ``scale0..`` por célula) o :class:`OpsCrops` (OPS, recortes TIFF enmascarados a la célula en fragmentos tar con desplazamientos en bytes en ``.index.csv`` y un archivo de escala por placa). Ambos dividen por una escala fija por placa y canal y recortan los valores, de modo que los recortes siguen sin procesar en disco; 2. las etiquetas y los folds: :func:`bbbc_fold_setup` (clases de MoA y los folds NSCB / NSC de :func:`spacr.well_set_training.moa_folds`) o :func:`ops_fold_setup` (clases génicas multietiqueta de las tablas de :mod:`spacr.gene_classes`, folds por gen, cabezas señuelo, el control barajado y el peso de pérdida por gen); 3. el muestreador (``train_balanced_sampling``): :class:`BalancedSampler`, uniforme por clase para BBBC021 y, para OPS, :func:`class_gene_sampler` (la mitad del lote de genes positivos, primero clase, luego gen y luego célula; la otra mitad de genes negativos); 4. el modelo (``train_arch``, :data:`IMAGE_ARCHITECTURES`): :func:`build_image_model` con la primera convolución adaptada al número de canales (:func:`adapt_first_conv`); 5. la transformación: :func:`transform_spec` registra todo el preprocesamiento, que se guarda con el fold y se vuelve a comprobar antes de puntuar (:func:`check_transform`, ítem 772). :class:`DevicePrep` la aplica en el dispositivo, con el aumento de datos del entrenamiento (diédrico, desplazamiento de hasta 4 px, ganancia por canal de 0.9 a 1.1); 6. :func:`train_image_fold` entrena con AdamW y un programa coseno (AMP en una GPU, reducción a la mitad del microlote cuando falta memoria) y puntúa las células reservadas; :func:`score_bbbc_run` puntúa una ejecución de BBBC021 por pocillo y por tratamiento.

records.label: spacr.gene_classes#0
records.source: Gene classes of a pooled screen, gene-grouped folds and the class-prediction benchmark.
records.translation: Clases génicas de un cribado agrupado, folds agrupados por gen y el banco de pruebas de predicción de clases.

records.context: A gene class is a set of screened genes that share an annotation: a kinase group, family or subfamily (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway, a GO-slim biological process, or a direction of one of Funk et al. 2022's per-gene feature scores. :func:`build_gene_classes` builds the class table from versioned source files (md5 recorded), merges or drops near-duplicate classes, and splits the genes into folds with multi-label iterative stratification (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), so every class has members in every fold and no gene is in two folds.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes#1
records.source: A gene class is a set of screened genes that share an annotation: a kinase group, family or subfamily (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway, a GO-slim biological process, or a direction of one of Funk et al. 2022's per-gene feature scores. :func:`build_gene_classes` builds the class table from versioned source files (md5 recorded), merges or drops near-duplicate classes, and splits the genes into folds with multi-label iterative stratification (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), so every class has members in every fold and no gene is in two folds.
records.translation: Una clase génica es un conjunto de genes cribados que comparten una anotación: un grupo, familia o subfamilia de quinasas (KinHub, Manning et al. 2002), un complejo CORUM, una ruta KEGG, un proceso biológico GO-slim o una dirección de una de las puntuaciones de características por gen de Funk et al. 2022. :func:`build_gene_classes` construye la tabla de clases a partir de archivos fuente versionados (con su md5 registrado), fusiona o descarta las clases casi duplicadas y divide los genes en folds con estratificación iterativa multietiqueta (Sechidis et al. 2011, :func:`grouped_multilabel_folds`), de modo que cada clase tiene miembros en cada fold y ningún gen está en dos folds.

records.context: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` fits one logistic regression per class on a gene-level feature table, fold by fold, with optional decoy heads (random gene sets of the classes' sizes, the null of the discovery calls) and a shuffled-class control. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` scores the out-of-fold predictions: per-class AUROC and average precision with bootstrap intervals, specificity against phenotype-positive and overlapping-class non-members, and the two discovery lists (known members with a new image phenotype; predicted new functions) at BH q < 0.05 against the decoy heads.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes#2
records.source: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` fits one logistic regression per class on a gene-level feature table, fold by fold, with optional decoy heads (random gene sets of the classes' sizes, the null of the discovery calls) and a shuffled-class control. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` scores the out-of-fold predictions: per-class AUROC and average precision with bootstrap intervals, specificity against phenotype-positive and overlapping-class non-members, and the two discovery lists (known members with a new image phenotype; predicted new functions) at BH q < 0.05 against the decoy heads.
records.translation: :func:`train_gene_class_baseline` ajusta una regresión logística por clase sobre una tabla de características a nivel de gen, fold a fold, con cabezas señuelo opcionales (conjuntos aleatorios de genes del tamaño de las clases, la distribución nula de las llamadas de descubrimiento) y un control de clases barajadas. :func:`evaluate_gene_class_run` puntúa las predicciones fuera del fold: AUROC y precisión media por clase con intervalos bootstrap, especificidad frente a no miembros con fenotipo positivo y no miembros de clases solapadas, y las dos listas de descubrimiento (miembros conocidos con un nuevo fenotipo de imagen; nuevas funciones predichas) con BH q < 0.05 frente a las cabezas señuelo.

Classes are then visited by source priority (kinase, CORUM, KEGG, GO-slim, Funk) and size; one whose members (or trainable members, without ``gene_class_merge``) overlap a kept class by ``gene_class_merge_jaccard`` is merged into it or dropped.
records.translation: Cada gen cribado anotado es miembro de su clase; los miembros entrenables son todos ellos o, con ``gene_class_gating``, solo los que tienen un fenotipo en el cribado. Después las clases se recorren por prioridad de fuente (quinasa, CORUM, KEGG, GO-slim, Funk) y tamaño; una cuyos miembros (o miembros entrenables, sin ``gene_class_merge``) se solapan con una clase conservada en ``gene_class_merge_jaccard`` se fusiona con ella o se descarta.

records.context: Score a gene-class run out of fold: per class, specificity, discovery and a summary.
records.label: spacr.gene_classes.evaluate_gene_class_run#0
records.source: Score a gene-class run out of fold: per class, specificity, discovery and a summary.
records.translation: Puntúa una ejecución de clases génicas fuera del fold: por clase, especificidad, descubrimiento y un resumen.

records.context: Per class (and decoy head) the positives are the held-out trainable members and the negatives every scored non-member; AUROC and AP with bootstrap intervals, AUROC against control pseudo-genes, against phenotype-positive non-members and against members of overlapping classes, for members unique to the class, and for members with and without a screening experiment phenotype. A class is specific when its AUROC interval is above 0.5 and both specificity AUROCs are above 0.5. Discovery: each head is z-scored over genes; with 100 or more size-matched decoy heads a gene's p value is its rank on the decoy heads (the gene-wise null), else against the pooled decoy z; BH within each type: (a) members without a screening experiment phenotype that score as members (a new image phenotype), (b) non-members of a specific class whose best class it is (a predicted new function).
records.label: spacr.gene_classes.evaluate_gene_class_run#1
records.source: Per class (and decoy head) the positives are the held-out trainable members and the negatives every scored non-member; AUROC and AP with bootstrap intervals, AUROC against control pseudo-genes, against phenotype-positive non-members and against members of overlapping classes, for members unique to the class, and for members with and without a screen phenotype. A class is specific when its AUROC interval is above 0.5 and both specificity AUROCs are above 0.5. Discovery: each head is z-scored over genes; with 100 or more size-matched decoy heads a gene's p value is its rank on the decoy heads (the gene-wise null), else against the pooled decoy z; BH within each type: (a) members without a screen phenotype that score as members (a new image phenotype), (b) non-members of a specific class whose best class it is (a predicted new function).
records.translation: Por clase (y cabeza señuelo), los positivos son los miembros entrenables reservados y los negativos cada no miembro puntuado; AUROC y AP con intervalos bootstrap, AUROC frente a pseudogenes control, frente a no miembros con fenotipo positivo y frente a miembros de clases solapadas, para miembros exclusivos de la clase y para miembros con y sin fenotipo en el cribado. Una clase es específica cuando su intervalo de AUROC está por encima de 0.5 y ambos AUROC de especificidad superan 0.5. Descubrimiento: cada cabeza se estandariza en z sobre los genes; con 100 o más cabezas señuelo del mismo tamaño, el valor p de un gen es su rango en las cabezas señuelo (la distribución nula por gen); si no, frente al z señuelo agrupado; BH dentro de cada tipo: (a) miembros sin fenotipo en el cribado que puntúan como miembros (un nuevo fenotipo de imagen), (b) no miembros de una clase específica para los que esta es su mejor clase (una nueva función predicha).

records.context: Per fold the features are standardised on the training genes; for every class an L2 logistic regression (C = 1, balanced class weights) is fitted on its trainable members against the non-members (members that do not train are left out) and scores the held-out genes. records.source: Per fold the features are standardised on the training genes; for every class an L2 logistic regression (C = 1, balanced class weights) is fitted on its trainable members against the non-members (members that do not train are left out) and scores the held-out genes. A class with fewer than two training positives in a fold is not scored there.
records.translation: En cada fold, las características se estandarizan sobre los genes de entrenamiento; para cada clase se ajusta una regresión logística L2 (C = 1, pesos de clase equilibrados) con sus miembros entrenables frente a los no miembros (los miembros que no entrenan quedan fuera) y se puntúan los genes reservados. Una clase con menos de dos positivos de entrenamiento en un fold no se puntúa en él.

records.context: Learn gene-gene links and gene-to-category membership from screening experiment gene profiles.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#0
records.source: Learn gene-gene links and gene-to-category membership from screen gene profiles.
records.translation: Aprende enlaces gen-gen y la pertenencia de genes a categorías a partir de los perfiles génicos de un cribado.

records.context: An optical pooled screening experiment gives one profile per gene. Whether those profiles say something about gene function that the published interaction maps did not already know is judged here by two protocols, each with its controls:
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#1
records.source: An optical pooled screen gives one profile per gene. Whether those profiles say something about gene function that the published interaction maps did not already know is judged here by two protocols, each with its controls:
records.translation: Un cribado óptico agrupado da un perfil por gen. Si esos perfiles dicen algo sobre la función génica que los mapas de interacción publicados no sabían ya se juzga aquí con dos protocolos, cada uno con sus controles:

records.context: the **time split**: the model is trained on the gene-gene edges known in 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) and scored on the edges added since (``gene_graph_new_edges``), among every gene pair that was not a 2022 edge;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#2
records.source: the **time split**: the model is trained on the gene-gene edges known in 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) and scored on the edges added since (``gene_graph_new_edges``), among every gene pair that was not a 2022 edge;
records.translation: la **división temporal**: el modelo se entrena con las aristas gen-gen conocidas en 2022 (STRING v11.5, BioGRID 4.4.214, CORUM 3.0) y se puntúa con las aristas añadidas desde entonces (``gene_graph_new_edges``), entre todos los pares de genes que no eran una arista en 2022;

records.context: **held-out genes**: for fold ``k`` every edge and every category membership of the fold's genes is hidden; the model scores those genes against every gene and every category.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#3
records.source: **held-out genes**: for fold ``k`` every edge and every category membership of the fold's genes is hidden; the model scores those genes against every gene and every category.
records.translation: **genes reservados**: para el fold ``k`` se ocultan todas las aristas y todas las pertenencias a categorías de los genes del fold; el modelo puntúa esos genes frente a todos los genes y todas las categorías.

records.context: The steps, each callable on its own and all four in order by :func:`run_gene_graph` (what ``spacr-run gene_graph`` calls):
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#4
records.source: The steps, each callable on its own and all four in order by :func:`run_gene_graph` (what ``spacr-run gene_graph`` calls):
records.translation: Los pasos, cada uno invocable por separado y los cuatro en orden mediante :func:`run_gene_graph` (lo que llama ``spacr-run gene_graph``):

records.context: :func:`build_gene_graph` assembles the nodes (screening experiment genes and non-targeting pseudo-genes), the feature blocks with their missing indicators, the typed edges, the categories and the folds;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#5
records.source: :func:`build_gene_graph` assembles the nodes (screen genes and non-targeting pseudo-genes), the feature blocks with their missing indicators, the typed edges, the categories and the folds;
records.translation: :func:`build_gene_graph` ensambla los nodos (genes del cribado y pseudogenes no dirigidos), los bloques de características con sus indicadores de ausencia, las aristas tipadas, las categorías y los folds;

records.context: :func:`train_gene_graph` runs the models: a graph transformer (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), Hadamard logistic regression (``lr``) and a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding (``spectral``), plus the training-free baselines ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` and ``prior``, each over feature arms and under the controls ``shufX`` (features permuted among genes), ``shufY`` (labels relabelled by a gene permutation) and ``rewire`` (degree-preserving swaps);
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#6
records.source: :func:`train_gene_graph` runs the models: a graph transformer (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), Hadamard logistic regression (``lr``) and a Laplacian-eigenmap embedding (``spectral``), plus the training-free baselines ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` and ``prior``, each over feature arms and under the controls ``shufX`` (features permuted among genes), ``shufY`` (labels relabelled by a gene permutation) and ``rewire`` (degree-preserving swaps);
records.translation: :func:`train_gene_graph` ejecuta los modelos: un transformador de grafos (``gps``), GraphSAGE (``sage``), GCN (``gcn``), regresión logística de Hadamard (``lr``) y una incrustación por mapas propios del laplaciano (``spectral``), más las líneas base sin entrenamiento ``cosine``, ``adamicadar`` y ``prior``, cada uno sobre brazos de características y bajo los controles ``shufX`` (características permutadas entre genes), ``shufY`` (etiquetas reasignadas mediante una permutación de genes) y ``rewire`` (intercambios que conservan el grado);

records.context: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` writes the time-split and held-out metrics, the per-fold summaries, the ablation table and the paired fold deltas;
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#7
records.source: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` writes the time-split and held-out metrics, the per-fold summaries, the ablation table and the paired fold deltas;
records.translation: :func:`evaluate_gene_graph` escribe las métricas de la división temporal y de genes reservados, los resúmenes por fold, la tabla de ablaciones y las diferencias pareadas por fold;

records.context: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibrates the out-of-fold scores, controls the false discovery rate with the non-targeting pseudo-genes as decoys and writes the explained prediction lists.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#8
records.source: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibrates the out-of-fold scores, controls the false discovery rate with the non-targeting pseudo-genes as decoys and writes the explained prediction lists.
records.translation: :func:`predict_gene_functions` calibra las puntuaciones fuera del fold, controla la tasa de falsos descubrimientos con los pseudogenes no dirigidos como señuelos y escribe las listas de predicciones explicadas.

records.context: The models are plain PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn. They run on the device named by ``gene_graph_device``; a CUDA device that is not available falls back to the CPU. On CUDA, the card rule of the shared workstation applies: a processing session waits until the card total plus its cap stays below ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` for ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` seconds, yields (saving a resume file) when the card goes over the limit, and stops when ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` GPU hours are used. On the CPU the computation is deterministic, so a rerun from the saved settings file writes the same tables.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph#9
records.source: The models are plain PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn. They run on the device named by ``gene_graph_device``; a CUDA device that is not available falls back to the CPU. On CUDA, the card rule of the shared workstation applies: a run waits until the card total plus its cap stays below ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` for ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` seconds, yields (saving a resume file) when the card goes over the limit, and stops when ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` GPU hours are used. On the CPU the computation is deterministic, so a rerun from the saved settings file writes the same tables.
records.translation: Los modelos son PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy y scikit-learn simples. Se ejecutan en el dispositivo indicado por ``gene_graph_device``; un dispositivo CUDA no disponible recurre a la CPU. En CUDA se aplica la regla de tarjeta de la estación de trabajo compartida: una ejecución espera hasta que el total de la tarjeta más su límite se mantenga por debajo de ``gene_graph_gpu_limit_gb`` durante ``gene_graph_admission_hold_s`` segundos, cede la tarjeta (guardando un archivo de reanudación) cuando la tarjeta supera el límite y se detiene cuando se han usado ``gene_graph_gpu_budget_h`` horas de GPU. En la CPU el cálculo es determinista, de modo que una nueva ejecución desde el archivo de configuración guardado escribe las mismas tablas.

records.label: spacr.gene_graph.GeneGraphModel#1
records.source: All share the decoders: pairs by DistMult, ``s(u, v) = scale * sum(z_u * r * z_v) + b``, and categories by ``scale * (z_g * q) @ z_c + b_c``. For ``lr`` the encoder is the raw concatenation of the blocks and their indicators, so the pair score is Hadamard logistic regression and the category head is linear.
records.translation: Todos comparten los decodificadores: pares mediante DistMult, ``s(u, v) = scale * sum(z_u * r * z_v) + b``, y categorías mediante ``scale * (z_g * q) @ z_c + b_c``. Para ``lr`` el codificador es la concatenación directa de los bloques y sus indicadores, de modo que la puntuación de pares es una regresión logística de Hadamard y la cabeza de categorías es lineal.

records.context: Per epoch (graph models), ``node_mask`` of the supervisable genes are node-masked (held-out tasks) and ``edge_mask`` of the other training edges are hidden and supervised; negatives are ``neg_per_pos`` per positive, half uniform and half degree-proportional, never a known pair. ``lr`` supervises every training edge (a minibatch of positives) and every training gene. Early stopping on the inner validation keeps the best state. The final scoring graph holds every training edge with the validation genes restored; test genes stay isolated. Every epoch draws from ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` and the resume file carries the torch random state, so a resumed run scores like an uninterrupted one.
records.label: spacr.gene_graph.run_config#1
records.source: Per epoch (graph models), ``node_mask`` of the supervisable genes are node-masked (held-out tasks) and ``edge_mask`` of the other training edges are hidden and supervised; negatives are ``neg_per_pos`` per positive, half uniform and half degree-proportional, never a known pair. ``lr`` supervises every training edge (a minibatch of positives) and every training gene. Early stopping on the inner validation keeps the best state. The final scoring graph holds every training edge with the validation genes restored; test genes stay isolated. Every epoch draws from ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` and the resume file carries the torch random state, so a resumed run scores like an uninterrupted one.
records.translation: En cada época (modelos de grafos), ``node_mask`` de los genes supervisables se enmascaran como nodos (tareas de genes reservados) y ``edge_mask`` de las demás aristas de entrenamiento se ocultan y se supervisan; los negativos son ``neg_per_pos`` por positivo, mitad uniformes y mitad proporcionales al grado, nunca un par conocido. ``lr`` supervisa cada arista de entrenamiento (un minilote de positivos) y cada gen de entrenamiento. La parada temprana sobre la validación interna conserva el mejor estado. El grafo de puntuación final contiene todas las aristas de entrenamiento con los genes de validación restaurados; los genes de prueba siguen aislados. Cada época extrae de ``default_rng([seed, s, epoch])`` y el archivo de reanudación lleva el estado aleatorio de torch, de modo que una ejecución reanudada puntúa como una ininterrumpida.

records.context: What a screen adds to gene-function prediction can only be stated against what prior protein knowledge alone predicts. This module builds that knowledge on the gene graph's node order (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): one row per screen gene and one per non-targeting pseudo-gene.
records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#1
records.source: What a screen adds to gene-function prediction can only be stated against what prior protein knowledge alone predicts. This module builds that knowledge on the gene graph's node order (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): one row per screen gene and one per non-targeting pseudo-gene.
records.translation: Lo que un cribado aporta a la predicción de funciones génicas solo puede establecerse frente a lo que predice por sí solo el conocimiento previo de proteínas. Este módulo construye ese conocimiento en el orden de nodos del grafo génico (:mod:`spacr.gene_graph`): una fila por gen del cribado y una por pseudogén no dirigido.

records.context: No hosted model or API is used. Models run from local Hugging Face weights (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); they are downloaded only when ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` is on. Every step can instead reuse the stored output of an earlier run (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), which is how a processing session is repeated without a GPU.
records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#10
records.source: No hosted model or API is used. Models run from local Hugging Face weights (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); they are downloaded only when ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` is on. Every step can instead reuse the stored output of an earlier run (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), which is how a run is repeated without a GPU.
records.translation: No se usa ningún modelo alojado ni ninguna API. Los modelos se ejecutan a partir de pesos locales de Hugging Face (``gene_knowledge_models_dir``); solo se descargan cuando ``gene_knowledge_allow_download`` está activado. Cada paso puede reutilizar en cambio la salida guardada de una ejecución anterior (``*_embeddings``, ``*_outputs``, ``foldseek_alignments``), que es como se repite una ejecución sin GPU.

records.context: :func:`fetch_protein_annotations`: UniProt sequences, Pfam / InterPro cross-references and function text, current (REST, batches of at most 100 accessions) and from an archived Swiss-Prot release (``.dat`` streamed out of the release tarball); plus a seeded draw of reviewed human proteins outside the library, the decoys' knowledge;
records.label: spacr.gene_knowledge#2
records.source: :func:`fetch_protein_annotations`: UniProt sequences, Pfam / InterPro cross-references and function text, current (REST, batches of at most 100 accessions) and from an archived Swiss-Prot release (``.dat`` streamed out of the release tarball); plus a seeded draw of reviewed human proteins outside the library, the decoys' knowledge;

records.source: Reads the merged arrays of ``translocation_merged_folder`` (or ``<src>/merged``). With ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` above 0 a five-plane array ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` gets its cell plane from the nuclei first (:func:`nucleus_territories`) and becomes the six-plane layout; a six-plane array already has its cell plane (Make Masks grows the territories itself with the same setting) and is read as it is. Cells are marked ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory when the territories were grown here or the merged folder's plane layout says Make Masks grew them; the territories are not cell outlines. Then :func:`translocation_cells` per field and :func:`translocation_summary`, written to ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, the summary tables, reference_curve.csv when ``translocation_reference`` names a reference curve table, and the translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles figure of :func:`translocation_figure`).
records.translation: Lee las matrices fusionadas de ``translocation_merged_folder`` (o ``<src>/merged``). Con ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` por encima de 0, una matriz de cinco planos ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` recibe primero su plano celular a partir de los núcleos (:func:`nucleus_territories`) y pasa a la disposición de seis planos; una matriz de seis planos ya tiene su plano celular (Make Masks expande los territorios por sí mismo con el mismo ajuste) y se lee tal cual. Las células se marcan con ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory cuando los territorios se expandieron aquí o la disposición de planos de la carpeta fusionada indica que los expandió Make Masks; los territorios no son contornos celulares. Después vienen :func:`translocation_cells` por campo y :func:`translocation_summary`, escritos en ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, las tablas de resumen, reference_curve.csv cuando ``translocation_reference`` nombra una tabla de curva de referencia, y la figura translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles de :func:`translocation_figure`).

records.context: For every field in ``<mask_src>/nucleus_mask_stack`` the nuclei under ``min_nucleus_size`` pixels are removed and the rest grow by up to ``expand_px`` pixels (:func:`nucleus_territories`). The territories are written to ``<mask_src>/cell_mask_stack`` and the kept nuclei to ``<mask_src>/nucleus_territory_seed_stack``, both as ``.npy`` in the nucleus mask's dtype, so the merged arrays carry a cell image layer, the nucleus image layer holds the nuclei the territories grew from, and Measure reads them like any other cell mask.
records.label: spacr.host_pathogen.write_nucleus_territories#1
records.source: For every field in ``<mask_src>/nucleus_mask_stack`` the nuclei under ``min_nucleus_size`` pixels are removed and the rest grow by up to ``expand_px`` pixels (:func:`nucleus_territories`). The territories are written to ``<mask_src>/cell_mask_stack`` and the kept nuclei to ``<mask_src>/nucleus_territory_seed_stack``, both as ``.npy`` in the nucleus mask's dtype, so the merged arrays carry a cell plane, the nucleus plane holds the nuclei the territories grew from, and Measure reads them like any other cell mask.
records.translation: Para cada campo de ``<mask_src>/nucleus_mask_stack`` se eliminan los núcleos de menos de ``min_nucleus_size`` píxeles y el resto se expande hasta ``expand_px`` píxeles (:func:`nucleus_territories`). Los territorios se escriben en ``<mask_src>/cell_mask_stack`` y los núcleos conservados en ``<mask_src>/nucleus_territory_seed_stack``, ambos como ``.npy`` con el dtype de la máscara nuclear, de modo que las matrices fusionadas llevan un plano celular, el plano nuclear contiene los núcleos a partir de los que crecieron los territorios, y Measure los lee como cualquier otra máscara celular.

records.context: ``'logistic'`` standardises the features on the training fold and fits a multinomial L2 logistic regression (C = 1). ``'xgboost'`` fits XGBoost with :data:`XGBOOST_PARAMS` on the CPU (:func:`spacr.ml._xgboost_cpu_safe`). ``'lda'`` is scikit-learn's linear discriminant analysis with its defaults, ``'shrinkage_lda'`` the same with the lsqr solver and Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, ``'knn'`` standardised features and five nearest neighbours, and ``'cpa_<name>'`` one of the CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 machine-learning classification models built as CPA builds it (:func:`spacr.cpa_classifiers.make_cpa_model`). records.translation: ``'logistic'`` estandariza las características en el fold de entrenamiento y ajusta una regresión logística multinomial L2 (C = 1). ``'xgboost'`` ajusta XGBoost con :data:`XGBOOST_PARAMS` en la CPU (:func:`spacr.ml._xgboost_cpu_safe`). ``'lda'`` es el análisis discriminante lineal de scikit-learn con sus valores predeterminados, ``'shrinkage_lda'`` lo mismo con el solucionador lsqr y la contracción de Ledoit-Wolf, ``'knn'`` características estandarizadas y cinco vecinos más cercanos, y ``'cpa_<name>'`` uno de los clasificadores de CellProfiler Analyst 3.0.5 construido como lo construye CPA (:func:`spacr.cpa_classifiers.make_cpa_model`). records.context: any of ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` and ``"decode"``, run in that order. A phase left out reads what it needs from the database, so a microplate sample position can be stitched once and decoded again. The alpha phenotype path adds ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` and ``"aggregate"``, run only when named here and after those four; ``ph_flatfield`` builds the laboratory microplate's maps once, before the microplate sample positions, and ``ph_masks`` writes each cell's microscope field of view-edge flags and flat-microscope field of view gains from the saved masks. A processing session of only these needs ``dst_root`` and ``plate`` but no ``genotype_source``, takes its microplate sample positions from ``ops_phenotype``, and adds to each microplate sample position's ``ops_report.json`` rather than replacing it. ``aggregate`` pools the microplate sample positions run and writes ``ops_guides_<plate>`` and ``ops_genes_<plate>``. ``"ph_merged"`` (per microplate sample position, after ``merge``) writes each microscope field of view to ``merged/`` (:func:`_ph_merged`); ``"ph_tables"`` (after ``aggregate``) writes the standard ``measurements/measurements.db`` tables (:func:`_ph_tables`); ``"ph_crops"`` cuts raw extracted image regions of owned cells into a sharded store (:func:`_ph_crops`). ``"ph_ownership"`` (per microplate sample position, after ``ph_masks``) finds the copies of each cell across overlapping microscope fields of view (:func:`_ph_cross_field_ownership`). ``"report"``, last, writes the yield funnel and the counts against a published table to ``results/ops_report/`` (:func:`_ph_report`). With ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` set, each microplate sample position's second phenotype acquisition is registered before its microscope fields of view are read (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). The alpha ``decode_qc`` phase (items 876 and 877) fits the false-call model and the genotype confidence over the microplate sample positions decoded, writing ``results/ops_decode_qc``; it also executes after ``decode`` when ``ops_decode_qc`` or ``ops_genotype_confidence`` is on. The alpha ``compare_calls`` phase (item 878) matches spaCR's calls to other workflows' per-cell tables (``ops_compare_tables``) and writes ``results/ops_compare``; it also executes after ``decode`` when those tables are set. The alpha profile path, ``"profile"`` and ``"evaluate"``, runs alone: it turns the stored cell tables of ``ops_profile_cells`` into gene profiles and scores them against reference gene pairs (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` builds the module atlas of those profiles (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) and ``"mitocarta"`` scores clusterings against MitoCarta and an external module table (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); like the profile path, both hold the BLAS and OpenMP pools to one thread while ``ops_deterministic_blas`` is on (the result's ``atlas_blas_threads``). ``"stress"``, after ``report``, times the finished store and writes ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` runs it too.

A phase left out reads what it needs from the database, so a well can be stitched once and decoded again. With ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` set, each well's second phenotype acquisition is registered before its fields are read (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). The alpha ``decode_qc`` phase (items 876 and 877) fits the false-call model and the genotype confidence over the wells decoded, writing ``results/ops_decode_qc``; it also runs after ``decode`` when ``ops_decode_qc`` or ``ops_genotype_confidence`` is on. The alpha ``compare_calls`` phase (item 878) matches spaCR's calls to other pipelines' per-cell tables (``ops_compare_tables``) and writes ``results/ops_compare``; it also runs after ``decode`` when those tables are set. The alpha profile path, ``"profile"`` and ``"evaluate"``, runs alone: it turns the stored cell tables of ``ops_profile_cells`` into gene profiles and scores them against reference gene pairs (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` builds the module atlas of those profiles (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) and ``"mitocarta"`` scores clusterings against MitoCarta and an external module table (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); like the profile path, both hold the BLAS and OpenMP pools to one thread while ``ops_deterministic_blas`` is on (the result's ``atlas_blas_threads``). ``"stress"``, after ``report``, times the finished store and writes ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` runs it too.
records.translation: cualquiera de ``"stitch"``, ``"phenotype"``, ``"objects"`` y ``"decode"``, ejecutadas en ese orden. Una fase omitida lee de la base de datos lo que necesita, de modo que un pocillo puede unirse una vez y volver a decodificarse. La ruta alfa de fenotipo añade ``"ph_flatfield"``, ``"ph_segment"``, ``"ph_measure"``, ``"ph_masks"``, ``"merge"`` y ``"aggregate"``, que solo se ejecutan cuando se nombran aquí y después de esas cuatro; ``ph_flatfield`` construye una vez los mapas de la placa, antes de los pocillos, y ``ph_masks`` escribe a partir de las máscaras guardadas los indicadores de borde de campo y las ganancias de campo plano de cada célula. Una ejecución solo con estas necesita ``dst_root`` y ``plate`` pero no ``genotype_source``, toma sus pocillos de ``ops_phenotype`` y amplía el ``ops_report.json`` de cada pocillo en lugar de sustituirlo. ``aggregate`` agrupa los pocillos ejecutados y escribe ``ops_guides_<plate>`` y ``ops_genes_<plate>``. ``"ph_merged"`` (por pocillo, tras ``merge``) escribe cada campo en ``merged/`` (:func:`_ph_merged`); ``"ph_tables"`` (tras ``aggregate``) escribe las tablas estándar de ``measurements/measurements.db`` (:func:`_ph_tables`); ``"ph_crops"`` corta recortes sin procesar de las células propias en un almacén fragmentado (:func:`_ph_crops`). ``"ph_ownership"`` (por pocillo, tras ``ph_masks``) encuentra las copias de cada célula entre campos solapados (:func:`_ph_cross_field_ownership`). ``"report"``, la última, escribe el embudo de rendimiento y los recuentos frente a una tabla publicada en ``results/ops_report/`` (:func:`_ph_report`). Con ``ops_ph_secondary_registration`` definido, la segunda adquisición de fenotipo de cada pocillo se registra antes de leer sus campos (:func:`_ph_secondary_shifts`). La fase alfa ``decode_qc`` (ítems 876 y 877) ajusta el modelo de llamadas falsas y la confianza del genotipo sobre los pocillos decodificados y escribe ``results/ops_decode_qc``; también se ejecuta tras ``decode`` cuando ``ops_decode_qc`` o ``ops_genotype_confidence`` está activado. La fase alfa ``compare_calls`` (ítem 878) empareja las llamadas de spaCR con las tablas por célula de otras canalizaciones (``ops_compare_tables``) y escribe ``results/ops_compare``; también se ejecuta tras ``decode`` cuando esas tablas están definidas. La ruta alfa de perfiles, ``"profile"`` y ``"evaluate"``, se ejecuta sola: convierte las tablas de células guardadas de ``ops_profile_cells`` en perfiles génicos y los puntúa frente a pares de genes de referencia (:func:`spacr.ops_tvn.run_profile_phases`); ``"modules"`` construye el atlas de módulos de esos perfiles (:func:`spacr.ops_modules.run_module_phase`) y ``"mitocarta"`` puntúa agrupamientos frente a MitoCarta y una tabla de módulos externa (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.run_mitocarta_benchmark`); como la ruta de perfiles, ambas mantienen los grupos de BLAS y OpenMP en un hilo mientras ``ops_deterministic_blas`` está activado (el ``atlas_blas_threads`` del resultado). ``"stress"``, tras ``report``, cronometra el almacén terminado y escribe ``results/ops_stress/stress_test.csv`` (:func:`spacr.ops_run_infra.stress_rows`); ``ops_stress_report`` también lo ejecuta.

records.label: spacr.ops_modules#0

records.translation: Módulos génicos de un cribado óptico agrupado: clústeres de consenso con un núcleo conocido.

records.context: A module is a cluster of the reference clustering that is anchored by known biology (a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway or a GO-slim term enriched in it), together with the genes the screen places next to that core although no resource links them to it. The atlas is built in three steps.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#1
records.source: A module is a cluster of the reference clustering that is anchored by known biology (a CORUM complex, a KEGG pathway or a GO-slim term enriched in it), together with the genes the screen places next to that core although no resource links them to it. The atlas is built in three steps.
records.translation: Un módulo es un clúster del agrupamiento de referencia anclado en biología conocida (un complejo CORUM, una ruta KEGG o un término GO-slim enriquecido en él), junto con los genes que el cribado sitúa junto a ese núcleo aunque ningún recurso los vincule con él. El atlas se construye en tres pasos.

records.context: 1. **Partitions.** The gene profiles (targeting genes with more than ten cells, plus the control guides grouped at random into pseudo-genes of four, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) are clustered once with PHATE + Leiden (seed 42) at the resolutions of :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (about 70, 250 and 500 clusters), and again ``ops_modules_runs`` times on resampled rows and guides (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). By default the profiles are standardised and reduced to the components holding 99 % of the variance first. With ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` the profile columns are used as they are, which is what a weighted profile (contrastive weighting) needs: standardising it again would undo the weighting. 2. **Anchoring.** In every reference cluster, a one-sided Fisher test for every group of 3 to 500 clustered genes, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster; the best group with q < 0.05 and three or more cluster genes is the anchor and its cluster genes are the known core. 3. **Data-selection boundaries.** A gene not linked to the core (no STRING v12 link of 0.4 or more, no BioGRID physical interaction, no shared enriched group) is a stable new member when its co-membership with the core over the consensus runs is above 0.5 and above the 99th percentile of both the control pseudo-genes and 500 fitness-matched random genes, its mean cosine to the core is above that of 1,000 fitness-matched genes (p < 0.01), at least three of its four guides point at the core, and its guides carry no specificity flag.
records.label: spacr.ops_modules#2
records.source: 1. **Partitions.** The gene profiles (targeting genes with more than ten cells, plus the control guides grouped at random into pseudo-genes of four, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) are clustered once with PHATE + Leiden (seed 42) at the resolutions of :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (about 70, 250 and 500 clusters), and again ``ops_modules_runs`` times on resampled rows and guides (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). By default the profiles are standardised and reduced to the components holding 99 % of the variance first. With ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` the profile columns are used as they are, which is what a weighted profile (contrastive weighting) needs: standardising it again would undo the weighting. 2. **Anchoring.** In every reference cluster, a one-sided Fisher test for every group of 3 to 500 clustered genes, Benjamini-Hochberg within the cluster; the best group with q < 0.05 and three or more cluster genes is the anchor and its cluster genes are the known core. 3. **Gates.** A gene not linked to the core (no STRING v12 link of 0.4 or more, no BioGRID physical interaction, no shared enriched group) is a stable new member when its co-membership with the core over the consensus runs is above 0.5 and above the 99th percentile of both the control pseudo-genes and 500 fitness-matched random genes, its mean cosine to the core is above that of 1,000 fitness-matched genes (p < 0.01), at least three of its four guides point at the core, and its guides carry no specificity flag.
records.translation: 1. **Particiones.** Los perfiles génicos (genes dirigidos con más de diez células, más las guías control agrupadas al azar en pseudogenes de cuatro, :func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_rows`) se agrupan una vez con PHATE + Leiden (semilla 42) a las resoluciones de :data:`MODULE_RESOLUTIONS` (unos 70, 250 y 500 clústeres), y de nuevo ``ops_modules_runs`` veces sobre filas y guías remuestreadas (:func:`spacr.ops_clusters.consensus_run`). Por defecto, los perfiles se estandarizan primero y se reducen a los componentes que contienen el 99 % de la varianza. Con ``ops_modules_precomputed_embedding`` las columnas de perfil se usan tal cual, que es lo que necesita un perfil ponderado (ponderación contrastiva): estandarizarlo de nuevo desharía la ponderación. 2. **Anclaje.** En cada clúster de referencia, una prueba de Fisher unilateral para cada grupo de 3 a 500 genes agrupados, Benjamini-Hochberg dentro del clúster; el mejor grupo con q < 0.05 y tres o más genes del clúster es el ancla y sus genes del clúster son el núcleo conocido. 3. **Criterios.** Un gen no vinculado al núcleo (sin enlace STRING v12 de 0.4 o más, sin interacción física de BioGRID, sin grupo enriquecido compartido) es un miembro nuevo estable cuando su copertenencia con el núcleo a lo largo de las ejecuciones de consenso supera 0.5 y supera el percentil 99 tanto de los pseudogenes control como de 500 genes aleatorios ajustados por aptitud, su coseno medio con el núcleo supera al de 1,000 genes ajustados por aptitud (p < 0.01), al menos tres de sus cuatro guías apuntan al núcleo y sus guías no llevan ningún indicador de especificidad.

records.context: Cell and cytoplasm rows share ``(prcf, object_label)``; nucleus rows name their cell in ``cell_id``. A cell with several nuclei gets the features of its largest nucleus and ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; nuclei without a cell are not exported. The structured-data names are ``plate``, ``well`` (such as B02), ``site`` and ``Metadata_cell_id``; positions (centroids, bounding boxes, distance to the microscope field of view edge) are kept as ``Location_*`` columns so profile scorers skip them, and bookkeeping columns are dropped, as are the ``pathogen`` distance features a laboratory microplate without a pathogen table carries. Features are ``float32``.
records.label: spacr.screen_staging.export_plate_parquet#1
records.source: Cell and cytoplasm rows share ``(prcf, object_label)``; nucleus rows name their cell in ``cell_id``. A cell with several nuclei gets the features of its largest nucleus and ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; nuclei without a cell are not exported. The keys are ``plate``, ``well`` (such as B02), ``site`` and ``Metadata_cell_id``; positions (centroids, bounding boxes, distance to the field edge) are kept as ``Location_*`` columns so profile scorers skip them, and bookkeeping columns are dropped, as are the ``pathogen`` distance features a plate without a pathogen table carries. Features are ``float32``.
records.translation: Las filas de célula y de citoplasma comparten ``(prcf, object_label)``; las filas de núcleo nombran su célula en ``cell_id``. Una célula con varios núcleos recibe las características de su núcleo más grande y ``Metadata_n_nuclei``; los núcleos sin célula no se exportan. Las claves son ``plate``, ``well`` (como B02), ``site`` y ``Metadata_cell_id``; las posiciones (centroides, recuadros delimitadores, distancia al borde del campo) se conservan como columnas ``Location_*`` para que los evaluadores de perfiles las omitan, y se descartan las columnas de gestión, así como las características de distancia ``pathogen`` que lleva una placa sin tabla de patógenos. Las características son ``float32``.
